question: Does point-in-time independent wallet convergence from the frozen Robinhood cohort improve early token discovery versus the existing Alpha Lab champion after provenance, entity, sellability and winner-selection controls?

hypothesis.challenger: verified independent cohort wallets self-initiate economically meaningful buys in the same token within a bounded early window
hypothesis.champion: existing Alpha Lab / Moonshot discovery path
hypothesis.claim_if_passes: incremental discovery evidence only, not BUY authority

anti_leakage: No wallet score may use the candidate token's future outcome.
No cohort membership may change because a member catches a winner.
No token may be added retrospectively because it later pumps.
Missing or failed source data is UNKNOWN/DEGRADED, never absence.
Shared funding/control collapses wallets to one economic entity before convergence count.
Provider leaderboard/ranking is descriptive input only and cannot be treated as ground truth alpha.
kill_or_revise_if: apparent lift disappears after economic-entity collapse
lift is explained by already-pumped tokens
lead time is not positive versus champion
edge depends on one wallet or one token
wallet quality only looks strong under winner-conditioned selection
current_known_source_cautions: Public FOMO Radar pages explicitly show dust/gift classifications, proving raw transfers cannot be treated as buys.
Several pages state the local tape begins after some pre-existing holdings, so historical entry/PnL can be incomplete.
Third-party PnL representations materially disagree for some addresses; experiment membership and signals must not depend on headline PnL.
